DYNAMIC TEMPLATE • MOVING ARROWS & LIVE PACKETS
Indirect Prompt Injection: Why the Attack Path Looks Identical to the Safe Path
Same user, same request, same tools — only the external document differs. Model Armor or open-source guards (Llama Guard, NeMo Guardrails) scan it; architecture, not wording, contains it.
B. ATTACK PATH — HOSTILE DOCUMENT (THE DOCUMENT IS THE ATTACKER)
LLM treats the hidden text as
Screen every external document, email, and URL
for injection payloads and PII before it
reaches the model: Model Armor on Google
Cloud, or self-hosted Llama Guard / NeMo
The moment untrusted content enters, deterministic
code sets tainted=True and physically unmounts
send_email, db_write, and outbound webhooks — via
an ADK taint guard, a LangGraph state flag, or an
Any write after a tainted read requires a
signed human approval outside the LLM loop —
the model cannot forge it. Cloud IAP-signed
JWTs and Keycloak OIDC approvals both satisfy
An agent that has send_email physically unmounted while reading external PDFs cannot be tricked into sending email.
